bullets.title: MSFT: Dividend raised 7.7%; Hedgeye bullish on weakness; Copilot at 30M seats
bullets.body: MSFT raised its quarterly dividend to $0.98 from $0.91 (+7.7%). Hedgeye explicitly names Microsoft as a preferred opportunity on weakness, while Nadella's TMT conference commentary highlighted 30M paid Copilot seats out of 250-300M addressable enterprise workers and a hardware-agnostic, multi-model AI strategy (Nvidia + AMD + internal silicon).

bullets.title: META: Added to Citi 90-day upside catalyst watch ahead of Connect 9/23-24; Hedgeye bullish
bullets.body: Citi added META to its 90-Day Upside Catalyst Watch ahead of META Connect (9/23-24), expecting announcements on AI models (potential Watermelon release), Muse, and AR/VR glasses. META infrastructure head discussed Titan AI cluster and Hyperion 5GW targets; management confirmed compute viewed as 'asset we can monetize' with >$600B AI infrastructure spend through 2030. Hedgeye explicitly names META as a long. Hyperscaler basket up +9% QTD vs Semis down -28% QTD.

bullets.title: NVDA: Hedgeye near bearish TREND; Grace Blackwell at $16/GPU-hr; compute futures launching by year-end
bullets.body: Hedgeye identifies NVDA as one of the riskiest mega-cap tech names, with NVDA close to a bearish TREND signal. On the bull side, Nvidia CEO noted Grace Blackwell rental pricing at $16/GPU-hour (vs $5 a year ago), token-generation demand up 25x in under a year, and AI safety/testing emerging as a new compute growth vector. Cash-settled compute futures based on H100/B200/B300 chips expected from ICE/Nodal by early October and CME post-October 20th CFTC comment period.

bullets.title: BKNG OW/$230 PT, ABNB upgraded to EW/$170, EXPE downgraded to UW/$235 — MS coverage initiation
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley's Matt Cost assumes OTA coverage: BKNG Overweight at $230 PT (18x avg '27/'28 EPS) on global scale, 4.7M unique properties, and 60s% direct B2C mix. ABNB upgraded from Underweight to Equal-weight at $170 PT (26x '27/'28 EPS) on 90% direct traffic and improving product execution. EXPE downgraded to Underweight at $235 PT (10x '27/'28 EPS) citing less differentiated assets and execution concerns. EXPE -2.2% pre-market on the downgrade.

bullets.title: AMZN: Project Mercury targets 10x same-day fulfillment expansion to 1,000+ sites by 2031; CART -4%
bullets.body: Amazon's Project Mercury plans to expand same-day fulfillment from ~85 to 1,000+ facilities by 2031 ($6.8B capex 2026-27), with same-day volume targeted at 50% of fulfilled orders by 2035. Same-day customers add 3x more items and spend 80%+ more. CART fell 4.1% pre-market as COST expanded its Uber Eats partnership to 47 states (~600 locations), seen as incrementally negative for CART's white-label delivery position.

bullets.title: AMD: Targeting 50%+ server CPU share; Venice on 2nm with available TSMC supply
bullets.body: Wolfe TMT conference takeaway: AMD is targeting over 50% CPU server share; a 50%+ share of a $200B+ TAM would imply a $100B+ server CPU business. AMD's Venice launch on 2nm benefits from available TSMC supply. Hedgeye does not flag AMD specifically as a risk but notes memory rotating lower vs DRAM.

bullets.title: AVGO: Google take-or-pay LTA protects share; optical to drive growth; supply the key revenue limiter
bullets.body: Wolfe TMT: AVGO's Google deal includes a take-or-pay LTA making it difficult for Mediatek to gain meaningful share. AVGO concurs that MRVL's Google content is focused on XPU attach, not accelerators. Optical segment expected to drive growth; supply constraints — not demand — will be the primary revenue limiter.

bullets.title: INTC +3.7% pre-market on SK Hynix memory chip talks; Ohio facility partnership reports
bullets.body: SK Hynix is weighing a deal with Intel to produce memory chips in the US, with reports of early talks on leasing/partnering on Intel's Ohio facility. INTC and SK Hynix trading up 3.7% pre-market on the news.

bullets.title: DELL: +347% YTD, hitting 52-week high at $566.90; AAPL exploring enterprise server market with M8 Ultra
bullets.body: DELL hit a new 52-week high, up 347% YTD to $566.90. Separately, Apple is examining plans to enter the enterprise server market using M8 Ultra chips with potential Nvidia networking partnerships — a potential longer-term competitive threat to DELL and HPE in the enterprise server space.

bullets.title: CRM + NVDA launch Koa AI model for Agentforce; Slack bookings triple digits
bullets.body: Salesforce and Nvidia launched Koa, a specialized AI model built on Nemotron for CRM reasoning and Agentforce agents. Slack bookings grew triple digits last quarter, Salesforce's fastest-growing product. Salesforce/Anthropic CEOs estimate businesses currently capture only 5-10% of AI's value.

bullets.title: HUBS & INTU: Investor Days tomorrow (9/17) — watch for AI-driven growth/margin guidance
bullets.body: HUBS Investor Day starts 10:00 ET on 9/17 with slides expected; consensus focus is whether AI accelerates growth and margins. INTU Investor Day starts 11:00 ET on 9/17; has historically reaffirmed guidance at analyst meetings (last guided Q1 & FY on 8/25). Both events are key near-term catalysts.

bullets.title: GEV: Bernstein reiterates Buy; Laguna conference today; raised 2030 capacity target to 30 GW
bullets.body: Bernstein reiterated Buy on GEV, viewing it as a durable electrification play well beyond data centers — electrification equipment backlog exceeded $40B in Q2 (~3 years of revenues), with data center orders $5B in H1 (38% of electrification orders) and utility-driven 62%. GEV also raised its 2030 capacity target from 24 GW to 30 GW at the Laguna conference.

bullets.title: FSLR: Withdraws ITC TOPCon patent complaint but continues lawsuits vs CSIQ, JKS
bullets.body: First Solar voluntarily withdrew its Section 337 TOPCon patent complaint with the USITC, terminating that investigation. However, FSLR is continuing patent lawsuits against Canadian Solar (CSIQ), JinkoSolar (JKS), T1 Energy, and Trina Solar affiliates. The move follows the Trump Administration's national security action on polysilicon imports. Roth separately flags FSLR as a behind-the-meter power beneficiary for data centers.

bullets.title: ANET, SMCI, CSCO, LITE: Goldman Hardware Bus Tour in San Jose on 11/19 — invitation-only
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs is co-hosting an in-person Hardware Bus Tour in San Jose on November 19, 2026, with meetings with Arista Networks (ANET; Buy), Cisco Systems (CSCO; Neutral), Super Micro Computer (SMCI; Sell-rated), and Lumentum Holdings (LITE; not GS-covered). LITE also +2.5% pre-market on the broader semis/hardware rally.

bullets.title: FOXA dominates Q3 TV ratings with World Cup; streaming hits 49% of total TV viewing
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs Q3 broadcast tracker: FOXA holds 25 of the top 26 telecasts through World Cup presentations, driving prime time broadcast ratings +41% including sports. Streaming accounts for 49.0% of total TV viewing, up 3.4% m/m, with YouTube leading at 14.2%. Cable ratings through Sept 13 up 3%; WBD +1%, DIS +2%.

bullets.title: PSKY/WBD: Judge sets Oct 14-15 for antitrust settlement talks on Paramount-Warner merger
bullets.body: A federal judge ordered Paramount Skydance and 12 state AGs to hold settlement talks October 14-15 regarding antitrust challenges to the Warner Bros. Discovery merger. PSKY trading at $11.11, +$0.10.

bullets.title: GOOGL: Hedgeye flags failed TREND signal; MS notes AI seen as acquisition channel, not disintermediation
bullets.body: Hedgeye notes Google failed its TREND signal, placing it in the same cautious bucket as AMZN (recently flipped bearish TREND) and TSLA. Morgan Stanley's OTA initiation views AI as an acquisition channel for online travel, not a disintermediation threat — a mild positive read-through for Google's travel/search revenue.

bullets.title: CCL: Stifel reiterates Buy, citing attractive entry and underappreciated 2029 targets
bullets.body: Stifel reiterated its Buy rating on Carnival Corp (CCL), citing an attractive entry point and underappreciated 2029 financial targets. Separately, Hedgeye notes TSA throughput decelerated to -2.5% YoY vs +2.0% prior week, a near-term travel demand watch item for cruise operators.

bullets.title: DKNG: Citi says positioned for sports betting upside regardless of prediction-market legal outcome
bullets.body: Citi research notes DKNG and FanDuel are positioned for sports betting upside regardless of the legal outcome on prediction markets, given their established platforms and regulatory positioning.

bullets.title: ZG: Preliminary injunction denied; Chicago antitrust case moved to private arbitration
bullets.body: A federal court denied Zillow's motion for a preliminary injunction in its case against MRED and Compass related to the Chicago listings data feed. The case against MRED has been moved to private arbitration, with Zillow's claims against Compass on hold pending that outcome. Zillow is seeking treble damages and attorneys' fees.
